records.authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.habit: Tendrilled perennial vine, limestone stream bottoms
characters.leaves: Blades 2–10 cm long and 3–14 cm wide, 2–3 lobes generally deeper than P. lutea; small yellowish ocelli sometimes present; leaf stalk 1–3.5 cm with NO petiolar glands
characters.flowers: Flower stalk 1–3 cm with remote bracts, 1–3 mm long sometimes deciduous; sepals 10–12 mm, linear petals narrower than sepals; corona filaments purple near bases, outer tips knobbed
characters.fruit: Subglobose berry 8–10 mm long, black-purple at maturity; seeds about 3 mm

records.diagnosis: Small narrow peduncular bracts and knobbed outer corona tips separate glandless-petioled P. affinis from P. lutea
holds: Source distinguishes absent petiole glands; existing project notes abaxial blade nectaries, which are a distinct possible structure and require direct gland-location check
Potential similarity to P. lutea at leaf level; hold foliage-only photos

records.historical: No species treatment in 1999 flora, whose local key contains only four Passiflora
records.authority: Kew POWO and current genus accounts; previous site morphology research

characters.habit: Tendrilled, often dense soft-hairy perennial vine, foliage often unpleasant-smelling when rubbed
characters.leaves: Mostly three-lobed, variable and pubescent; species complex
characters.flowers: Five often whitish petals, multiseriate corona, surrounded by three deeply divided/sticky gland-tipped involucral bracts
characters.fruit: Berry generally round/ovoid; typical foetida often yellow-orange ripe, color highly dependent on infraspecific taxonomy
characters.habitat: Kew native at Texas state scale, tropical-subtropical American range

records.diagnosis: Highly divided bract cage around flower/fruit plus sticky glandular hairs; leaf and fruit alone cannot exclude nearby foetida-complex taxa
holds: No original 1999 species description: secondary source only
Complex with multiple varieties, confirm variety/plant record before claims about fruit color
Texas native statewide does NOT prove county BONAP inclusion
User-approved learner inclusion is separate from target-zone nativity

records.authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.habit: Vigorous tendrilled vine several metres long, often fencerows/stream bottoms
characters.leaves: Leaves 6–15 × 7–15 cm, three deep acute serrate lobes, undersides pubescent; petioles up to 8 cm bearing two glands near blade
characters.flowers: Very large showy bluish-lavender petals, 25–35 mm long; rarely white; large flower with layered corona
characters.fruit: Ovoid to nearly round, up to 50 mm, yellow-orange when ripe; seeds 4–5 mm

records.diagnosis: Two petiolar glands + serrate lobes + showy large purple corona and 5-cm maypop separate from small green-flowered species
holds: Older north-central flora county list primarily east of Hays; local BONAP distribution required
Do not infer cultivar or ornamental specimen is wild regional genotype

records.authority: Kew Plants of the World Online, accepted species; prior project morphology

characters.habit: Tendrilled passionflower associated with foetida complex
characters.leaves: Often more pointed/angular lobes than local foetida comparisons but variable
characters.flowers: Flowers surrounded by fine dissected bracts; pinkish shades possible but not definitive
characters.fruit: Ripe fruit often crimson/red in project comparisons; confirm species and maturity before diagnosis

records.diagnosis: Kew 2026 accepted separate species and lists historical variety as synonym; require multiple characters including ripe fruit and bract morphology
holds: Taxonomic split 2023 and legacy treatments still use P. foetida var. lanuginosa; keep sources distinct

records.authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.habit: Tendrilled perennial vine up to around 5 m, stream bottoms and hillside woods
characters.leaves: 3–7 cm long, 2–10 cm wide, usually broader than long, shallowly to moderately 3-lobed with broad blunt rounded entire lobes; petioles to 5 cm NO glands
characters.flowers: Flower stalks 1.5–4 cm, NO bracts; sepals 5–10 mm, petals present and smaller than sepals, outer corona tips not knobbed
characters.fruit: Purple-black when mature, globose-ovoid berry 8–15 mm long; seeds 4.5–5 mm

records.diagnosis: Glandless petiole, no floral bracts, rounded shallow lobes; unlike P. affinis bracted peduncles and knobbed corona
holds: Compare P. lutea vs P. affinis with preserved flowering stalk, not only small green flower

records.authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.habit: Tendrilled vine usually sprawling over limestone, occasionally climbing low shrubs
characters.leaves: Very narrow deeply divided lobes; two long lateral lobes and shorter central, western form further subdivided to apparent 7 lobes; underside glabrous, upper hairy
characters.petiole: Pair of sessile saucer-like glands where petiole joins blade 1–1.2 mm diameter
characters.flowers: Petals absent; five greenish sepals 6–10 × about 2 mm; short flower stalks 3–8 mm
characters.fruit: Black ripe globose berry 8–15 mm diameter; seeds 3–4 mm reticulate

records.diagnosis: Deeply cut narrow 'birdwing' leaves, paired saucer petiole glands and tiny petal-less flowers, unlike glandless P. lutea
holds: 1999 mentions two leaf morphotypes; do not split based only on lobing
Small flower sepal length 6–10 mm, NOT count of sepals
